model_solution:
1. Main phase 1: activate Gideon's +1. He becomes a 5/5 creature, which is 6/6 with the emblem. He has been under your control since the start of the turn, so he can attack.
2. Cast Illusory Wrappings on Gideon, using Farmland ×3. His base P/T becomes 0/2, which is 1/3 with the emblem. The Wrappings' timestamp is later than Gideon's +1, so it overrides his 5/5 base.
3. Cast Dead Weight on your Knight Ally token, using a Swamp. The Knight is 3/3 with the emblem, so it becomes 1/1.
4. Go to combat and attack with Gideon (1/3) and the Knight (1/1). Both have skulk from Behind the Scenes, so a creature with greater power can't block them. The opponent's creatures have power 4, 3 and 2, and all are greater than 1. Neither attacker can be blocked, so the opponent declares no blockers.
5. In the declare blockers step, cast Anguished Unmaking on Illusory Wrappings, using Farmland and 2 Swamps. Wrappings is exiled and you lose 3 life. Gideon is 6/6 again, since his +1 effect lasts until end of turn.
6. Combat damage: Gideon deals 6 and the Knight deals 1. That is 7 damage, which is lethal against the opponent's 7 life.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
Let me work out the board state: Gideon at 4 loyalty with his emblem active (+1/+1 to creatures we control), plus a Knight Ally token that shows as 2/2 but is actually 3/3 with the emblem bonus, and Behind the Scenes granting skulk plus a {4}{W} pump ability.

I'm counting mana: four Irrigated Farmland and three Swamp gives seven total. My hand holds Illusory Wrappings, Dead Weight, Temmet, and Anguished Unmaking, while the opponent sits at 7 life defending with a flying indestructible Seraph, a Sparring Mummy, and a sacrifice-prone Labyrinth Guardian.

Thinking through skulk: Gideon's +1 ability makes him a 6/6 indestructible creature with the emblem, but skulk only stops blockers with strictly greater power, so all three opposing creatures (power 4, 3, and 2) could still legally block him since their power is less than or equal to 6. I need to actually remove or neutralize blockers rather than rely on skulk alone, since equal-or-lower power creatures are still allowed to block.

Running the math: Dead Weight on the Guardian kills it outright via its sacrifice trigger for just 1 mana, Anguished Unmaking exiles the Seraph for 3, and Temmet for 2 can make a Knight token unblockable and bigger — that's 6 mana total, leaving the Mummy as the only blocker. But with the Mummy eating Gideon's attack, only the unblockable Knight's damage gets through, which isn't enough to close out 7 life, so I need to find a way to get two unblocked attackers through instead of one.

Illusory Wrappings doesn't remove Mummy, and Dead Weight only shrinks it to 1/1 rather than killing it, so that's only one answer solved. Maybe Gideon skips attacking and instead I make another Knight token before combat, giving a second 3/3 with the emblem bonus that Temmet's trigger could target.

Checking Temmet's combat trigger: Knight gets +1/+1 and unblockable for 4 damage, but I still need 3 more unless I skip Temmet since skulk already makes the Knight's power-3 body unblockable by anything with power over 3 — meaning Seraph (power 4) can't block it either, while Mummy and Guardian still can since their power is ≤3.

Trying Illusory Wrappings to shrink a blocker: putting it on Seraph reduces it to 0/2, letting it block anything. So I'm considering removing Guardian with Dead Weight and exiling Mummy with Unmaking, leaving Seraph as the only blocker capable of stopping anything power 4 or higher — but that still stops Gideon, using up 6 mana with only 1 left, and not getting through enough damage. Trying without Temmet instead: removing Guardian and exiling Mummy...

With Knight and Gideon attacking (Temmet and the new token are summoning sick), that's Knight 3 plus Gideon 6 for 9, and with Temmet's bonus Knight becomes 4 and unblockable. I just need Gideon to connect too — either its power beats a blocker or I pump it — within my 7 mana budget.

Actually, if I skip Temmet and just pump Gideon for 5 mana, it becomes 7 power, and since Seraph can't block it and I force through the other blockers, Gideon alone connects for exactly lethal.

That emblem path kills Gideon though, which stops him attacking. Let me check Temmet's ability instead: it targets a creature token to make it unblockable with +1/+1, which fits Knight perfectly since Gideon isn't a token. Running the math on pumping everyone +1/+1 for 5 mana combined with Temmet's unblockable Knight, I still seem to come up short on total damage and need to figure out how Gideon gets through blockers.

I'm checking other cards for relevance - Mummy's untap trigger, Labyrinth Guardian's sacrifice clause, Irrigated Farmland's cycling - none seem to help. Considering whether Dead Weight or Wrappings on opposing creatures could lower their power enough to let more of my attackers through unblocked, but that actually seems counterproductive since lower power lets them block more freely, not less.

With only two real attackers available (Knight and Gideon, since the Gideon token would have summoning sickness), and the opponent holding three blockers under a skulk-style restriction, I need to find a way to force lethal damage through regardless of how they assign blocks - possibly using an instant-speed pump or removal after blockers are declared, like Behind the Scenes or an Unmaking effect to strip away a blocker without granting trample.

Testing Gideon's -4 for a second emblem giving creatures +2/+2, then combining with Temmet and a pump spell to push Knight's power high enough, but the mana costs keep stacking up past what's available, so I'm trying different combinations of buffs to hit exactly seven damage unblocked.

Shifting to the skulk angle: since skulk lets a creature be blocked only by creatures with equal or lower power, I want Gideon's power kept low with Wrappings so none of the opponent's bigger creatures can block him.

But testing it out, using Wrappings and removal only gets me to 4 damage, short of 7. Without Wrappings, Gideon hits for 6, and removing Guardian and Mummy clears blockers except Seraph, which could still block Gideon alone.

Trying Temkit plus Wrappings: with Gideon down to 1 power, none of the creatures have low enough power to profitably block, since Guardian's 2, Mummy's 3, and Seraph's 4 all exceed it. That uses 5 mana for 5 damage total, leaving 2 mana unspent but needing more reach to close the gap to lethal.

I'm second-guessing whether Gideon's +1 ability and emblem can both be used this turn, and reconsidering whether Dead Weight should target Mummy instead, looking for a combination involving Temmet's trigger with Gideon that actually gets there.

Trying another angle: killing Temmet via Dead Weight to enable embalm costs too much mana, so I'm working through the math on unblocked damage instead — using Wrappings on Gideon to shrink his power while Knight slips through unblocked, tallying whether that combo plus remaining mana actually hits for enough damage.

Trying Temmet targeting another Knight token instead - but that doesn't help Gideon. Maybe using Wrappings on Gideon then pumping could still leave him short of power. Checking skulk from Behind the Scenes and mana constraints across Farmland and Swamps to see what colors are available for Temmet, Wrappings, Dead Weight, and Unmaking. Looking for a combination totaling 7 power unblocked between Gideon and Knight, with Knight made unblockable via Temmet and Gideon needing enough power on his own.

I'm considering whether Wrappings could overwrite Gideon's base power/toughness after his +1 ability turns him into a creature, since aura timestamps matter and Wrappings needs a creature to target—so it'd have to be cast after the activation.

Then I pivot away from that, wondering if making opponent's blockers bigger via Wrappings could help, but that doesn't fit since Wrappings sets base power/toughness low. I also briefly consider whether exiling Gideon via Unmaking or using his -4 emblem changes anything, before moving toward thinking about planeswalker damage prevention or cycling effects as another angle.

Library size doesn't matter here, so I refocus on making Knight unblockable through Temmet while using Gideon's -4 for a second emblem, running the math on total power versus mana available - it keeps coming up short by one pump or one unblocked attacker. I try splitting mana between pump and Temmet but still can't get both attackers through with only one ability activation per turn, so I start wondering if casting Temmet and then using Dead Weight on it does anything, before shifting to consider Dead Weight on Mummy instead.

I realize the emblem is irrelevant since it's the opponent's, and Dead Weight would just make Mummy a 1/1 - stacking Wrappings on top too seems unnecessary. I also rule out any "sacrifice when targeted" guardian trick since Temmet's trigger is an ability, not a spell targeting it. Then I reconsider whether Gideon even needs to attack, and start thinking about blocker math: to get Gideon through I'd need blockers whose power is high enough to not want to block, but Dead Weight and Wrappings only lower toughness/power in the wrong direction for that purpose - removing blockers entirely via Guardian looks like the more promising route.

I try combining Dead Weight on the Guardian, Anguished Unmaking on either Mummy or Seraph, and still come up short since one blocker always remains able to stop either Gideon or the Knight, capping damage at 4 no matter how I split removal. I test swapping Wrappings onto Gideon instead to drop his power so a leftover blocker can't block him, but that still nets the same 4 damage. I start wondering if there's a way to squeeze out more damage, considering Temmet's once-per-combat unblockable buff on a token, then pivot to trying Anguished Unmaking directly on Gideon's creature form instead.

I also think about timing tricks — pumping Gideon's power after blocks are already declared, so his low power (from Wrappings) makes him unblockable at the moment blocks lock in, then boosting him afterward — but that costs too much total mana. I try Dead Weight on Gideon alone to lower his power to 4, but that's still blockable by Seraph, Mummy, or the Guardian, so I start looking for another way to manipulate his power before blockers are assigned.

Checking land count: 4 Farmland plus 3 Swamp gives me 7 mana, not 8, so the full combo of Wrappings + Temmet + pump doesn't fit. I also consider whether Wrappings could target the Knight token instead, but its base stats don't help, and I start wondering if a second Knight attack via Temmet could close out the opponent's 7 life instead.

Trying combinations like Illusory Wrappings plus Dead Weight to kill Seraph or Mummy through toughness reduction, weighing the mana cost against just using Unmaking directly — seems less efficient but worth checking if it frees up removal for the Guardian.

Shifting focus to skulk and unblockable interactions: wondering if Behind the Scenes or Anguished Unmaking can be exiled or repurposed, then reconsidering Gideon's abilities — maybe a second Knight token from +1, or using -4 for the emblem alongside a skulk creature whose power is low enough to dodge Seraph's block.

Trying to total up 7 damage between Gideon and the Knight, since the Knight becomes unblockable via Temmet's trigger at 4/4, leaving Gideon needing to get through for 3 more against three blockers. Considering whether Wrappings could be removed after blocks via exiling it with Anguished Unmaking, returning Gideon to 6/6 for lethal — tallying the mana cost at 3 for Wrappings plus 3 for Unmaking.

What if I put Wrappings on Gideon first, then use Unmaking to remove the Wrappings after blockers are declared, bringing Gideon back to full power for lethal damage?

For the last point, I need Knight to get through too, but opponents can just block Knight with Guardian or Mummy. Killing Guardian with Dead Weight still leaves Mummy as a blocker, so that doesn't guarantee it. Swapping Dead Weight for Temmet doesn't quite reach six either — I'm still one short, so I need to find another angle.

Trying Knight with Wrappings instead doesn't quite work since there's only one copy of Wrappings available, so I'd need to split resources between Knight and Gideon differently and see if either becomes unblockable with enough power to finish the job.

Actually with Gideon alone plus Wrappings and Unmaking that's 6 mana, 6 damage, leaving opponent at 7 — I need 1 more. Dead Weight on Knight drops it to 1/1 but makes it unblockable since all blockers have power ≥2 against skulk, so Knight connects for exactly that last point: 6+1=7 total, using Wrappings (3) and Unmaking (3) plus 1 for Dead Weight.

Now I'm working out the mana base: three Swamps cover the double black needs (Dead Weight, Unmaking's B), while Farmlands supply U for Wrappings and W for Unmaking — four Farmland, three Swamp total should cover everything, so I'm double-checking Gideon's stats with Wrappings applied.

After the +1/+1 emblem, Wrappings makes Gideon 0/2 become 1/3, giving it skulk at power 1, which Dead Weight shrinks the Knight to 1/1 so nothing with power ≤1 can block since Seraph, Mummy, and Guardian all have higher power. I'm confirming Unmaking exiles Wrappings after blockers are declared (with none able to block), Gideon reverts to 6/6 for 7 total damage, and I still need to check whether Guardian's ability fizzles in this line.
